subject: Reserved commit: throughput guarantees, measurement window & discount structure

Cc: Procurement <procurement@quantahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool guarantees + discount ask (initial)

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here — QuantaHealth — is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for our clinical summarization pipeline. We have two asks up front: a) firm throughput guarantees for steady-state inference (we target ~1.2M tokens/day, with peak bursts up to 250 tokens/sec across concurrent sessions) and b) a committed pricing/discount structure for a 12-month reserved commit.

Attached is an excerpt from our RFP (QH_RFP_throughput_requirements.pdf) with expected request profile. High level:
- Baseline: 100 requests/sec, average 30 tokens/request (NLP extract + summarization);
- Peak bursts: 250 tokens/sec sustained for ~10 minutes during nightly batch windows;
- Latency objective: p95 < 300ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), p99 < 800ms for full flows;

We need simple guardrails in contract language: how you measure tokens/sec and requests/sec (synthetic vs production sampling), what happens on missed guarantees, and what discount/credit we can expect for a 12-month commit.

Can you share a measurement plan and a preliminary discount grid we can present to procurement? Aim to have a version we can review with our legal this week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of AI Platforms
QuantaHealth

Alex — appreciate the clear RFP. Attaching a concise proposal (redwood_dedicated_proposal_QH_v2.pdf) with an initial pricing / commit band and the measurement approach. Summary here:

Proposal highlights:
- Reserved commit: 6x A100-equivalent GPU months (committed monthly allocation) billed monthly for 12 months.
- Baseline guarantees: 1200 tokens/sec aggregate (across the pool) and 110 requests/sec steady-state; peak bursting supported up to pool capacity with soft throttling.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 850ms for the configured model/quantization profile.
- Credits: 10% of monthly bill for a single month where steady-state tokens/sec < 90% of guaranteed during a 24h verified window (see measurement).
- Discounts: 12-month commit -> 22% list discount; 24-month -> 28% (examples in attached).

Measurement methodology (short):
1) Measurement windows: run three 2-hour steady-state windows (canary -> pilot -> full) during mutually agreed dates.
2) Synthetic harness: we run synthetic request streams reflecting your request shape (tokens/request distribution, concurrency).
3) Production sampling: we correlate production telemetry during pilot to synthetic results (token counts, error rates, latencies).
4) Definition: steady-state is 95th percentile token/sec over 15-min buckets across the window.

I'll let Karthik flesh out the technical test plan (warm caches, KV prefixing, cold start handling). If Quanta wants stronger financial remediation, we can map higher credits to higher commit bands.

Ben
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

Alex / Ben — quick technical note to make the measurement clear and avoid surprises:

Measurement details (technical):
- Tokens/sec metric: we measure emitted model tokens (server-side) aggregated across GPU pool and expressed as a 15-minute rolling percentile. For guarantees we use the median of three 2-hour steady-state windows unless otherwise negotiated.
- Requests/sec: counted as completed inference requests/sec (success codes) during the window; retries excluded.
- Warm cache policy: KV cache is warmed at the start of the first window; we include a 15-minute ramp to avoid cold-start noise.
- Concurrency profile: we will replay your telemetry distribution (attached sample) to ensure headroom for concurrent sessions.
- Latency measurement: p95/p99 taken on server-side end-to-end (request arrival to final token emitted) including queueing.
- Fault handling: transient infra events (provider-maintenance, scheduled host reboots) will be excluded if declared ahead of test; otherwise they count against the window.

Test artifacts we'll provide back: raw per-second time series (tokens/sec, rps, latency buckets), config used for the harness, and a replay script. If you want, we can add a third-party observer (mutual canary) to validate.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool guarantees + discount ask (initial)

Alex — wanted to add a commercial guardrail and a simple escalation path so procurement has something to sign off on quickly. Proposed edits to the credit/discount table:

- Commit band A (6 GPU-months): 18% discount, 5% monthly credit if tokens/sec < 85% across the agreed measurement windows (single-month cap)
- Commit band B (12 GPU-months): 24% discount, 10% monthly credit if tokens/sec < 90% across the measurement windows
- Commit band C (24+ GPU-months): 30% discount, 15% monthly credit + 30-day remediation window (Redwood performs corrective capacity actions before credit is applied)

Also proposing a 21-day acceptance window post-deployment for the measurement runs and a single production canary at 25% traffic before full switch. That reduces legal friction.

If Quanta is comfortable with the Commit band B numbers we can route this to contracts (I will include an explicit measurement appendix).

Neha
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

1) Measurement window timing: we prefer the first canary/pilot week to be during our low-traffic window (Mar 9-13). Will that work for Redwood's infra?
2) Remediation: for Commit band B we want credits to be netted against the following invoice (not refunded).
3) Test observer: procurement would like a short summary from the synthetic harness plus the raw time-series CSVs. Please confirm you will provide both.

If you can confirm these three points and send the measurement appendix by EOD Monday (Mar 2), we'll get contracts started.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Alex
